title: Exclusive: Bewakoof Cofounder Prabhkiran Singh Launches AI Shopping Assistant Save8
summary: Bewakoof cofounder Prabhkiran Singh launches AI-powered shopping assistant Save8
detailed: Bewakoof cofounder and former CEO Prabhkiran Singh has launched Save8, an AI-powered shopping assistant for comparing prices and offers across ecommerce and quick commerce platforms.

Bewakoof cofounder and former CEO Prabhkiran Singh has launched Save8, an AI-powered shopping assistant that helps consumers compare prices and offers across ecommerce and quick commerce platforms.
The venture comes months after Singh stepped down from Bewakoof, the D2C fashion brand he led for nearly 14 years.
Singh is also looking to raise external capital for Save8 and has held talks with investors, including All In Capital, sources told Inc42.
The proposed funding amount and the final investor lineup could not be ascertained.
Questions sent to Singh about Save8’s launch, business model, and fundraising plans remained unanswered till the time of publication.
According to its website, Save8 aggregates prices and offers across more than 1,000 online stores.
It compares product prices alongside coupons, cashback, discounted gift cards, and bank offers to help shoppers identify potential savings.

Users can compare offers by pasting a product link into Save8’s website, adding ‘save8.ai/’ before the product URL in their browser’s address bar, or sending the link to the Save8 app through a shopping app’s share menu.
The platform lists Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Zepto, Blinkit, and Swiggy Instamart among the services it covers.
Its comparison tools aim to help users assess purchase costs after accounting for available discounts and payment offers.
Save8 is available through its website and mobile applications.
Its Google Play listing says it displays available bank and payment offers but does not automatically apply them.
Save8 operates under ThousandX Ventures LLP, according to its terms of service.
Besides its deal-finding tools, Save8 facilitates the purchase of digital gift cards issued by brands or their authorised partners.
Singh cofounded Bewakoof in 2012.
In February this year, he announced plans to step down as CEO at the end of March, citing personal priorities, including health and family.
His departure ended a nearly 14-year stint at the company.
Aditya Birla Group’s digital-first venture TMRW invested ₹200 Cr to acquire a majority stake in Bewakoof, with the transaction completed in February 2023.
During Singh’s tenure, Bewakoof built a youth-focused fashion business catering to millennials and Gen Z shoppers, expanding beyond its own D2C platform into online marketplaces and offline retail.
With Save8, Singh is moving from selling consumer products to helping shoppers compare where and how to buy them.
